tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Pipeline routing validates metadata against the routing graph, not just the final estimator. validate_metadata rejects names routed to no object (sklearn/utils/_metadata_requests.py:1110-1124). At a consumer, True forwards a requested value, False ignores it, and None records a supplied value as unrequested for an error (lines 461-474). Intermediate steps may request sample_weight even when the final estimator does not. Explicit requests avoid silently passing metadata to the wrong consumer; missing support and an unset request are distinct cases.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: NearestCentroid wraps decision_function, predict_proba and predict_log_proba with available_if(_check_euclidean_metric); the predicate checks metric == "euclidean" (sklearn/neighbors/_nearest_centroid.py:337-350). The descriptor raises AttributeError when the predicate fails, so hasattr on a Manhattan-configured instance is false (sklearn/utils/_available_if.py:27-44). This makes availability metric-dependent. The discriminant implementation is designed for Euclidean scoring; squaring a non-Euclidean distance is mathematically possible but does not establish the same model.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The "cv_object" constraint expands to _CVObjects, whose predicate accepts any of its integer>=2, split/get_n_splits, iterable-not-string, or None alternatives (sklearn/utils/_param_validation.py:735-744). validate_parameter_constraints accepts a parameter when one constraint passes and otherwise raises InvalidParameterError. BaseEstimator._validate_params directly delegates to that validator (sklearn/base.py:463-475); _fit_context supplies the skip-validation and fitted-partial_fit guards before calling it (lines 1351-1359). Thus the boolean is consumed by validation rather than returned as the fit result.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: There is no mismatch with a default argument contract: LogisticRegression.fit explicitly supplies accept_large_sparse=solver not in ["liblinear", "sag", "saga"] to validate_data (sklearn/linear_model/_logistic.py:1249-1257). Those solvers therefore reject unsupported large sparse indices, while the other paths allow them. A validator default of True does not promise that every estimator using the validator accepts 64-bit indices.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: HTTP 412 is treated as an OpenML application error, so the network retry wrapper immediately re-raises it rather than sleeping and retrying (sklearn/datasets/_openml.py:97-113). The JSON API helper converts it to OpenMLError (lines 246-255). Name/version lookup can then try a deactivated-dataset URL (lines 337-350), adding another request when the fallback is needed. These are concrete control-flow and network-cost implications; the code provides no measurement that Python exception overhead is significant at scale and does not establish cascading failure behavior.
